A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, and their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The earlier appendices E–G are retained as I–K in v2, alongside new appendices E–H.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention-knockout, answer-probability, and module-ablation experiments on six GQA task types across LLaVA models, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds visual-token filtering, inference-efficiency, dense-caption comparison, and OKVQA/AOKVQA results in appendices E–H.

M1.justification: The attention-knockout, module-ablation, and logit-lens procedures are retained. Appendix F adds a limited inference adaptation that removes image tokens from upper layers of LLaVA-v1.6-13B to reduce computation.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained six GQA task types, Appendix H evaluates OKVQA and AOKVQA, extending coverage to questions requiring external commonsense and world knowledge. Appendix G also introduces a text-only scenario using Visual Genome dense captions in place of images.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons are retained. Figure 14 adds unmodified LLaVA-v1.6-13B as the control for the token-removal variant, while Appendix G adds an evaluated unimodal Vicuna-v1.5-13B comparison with the multimodal information-flow findings.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce distinct protocols: excluding patches with norms above 57 from the intervention groups, replacing images with dense captions, and sweeping token removal over the final 5–35 layers while measuring accuracy and runtime. These extend the evaluation design substantially; the original GQA sampling and attention-knockout settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted test of whether high-norm patches carrying global information explain the region-specific findings, an accuracy/runtime sensitivity analysis for token removal, and a comparison of information routing with caption inputs. These address robustness, practical applicability, and modality-specific mechanisms beyond the retained ablations.

E5.justification: Shaded bands already appear in v1's plots and continue in v2. Neither version defines their statistical meaning or reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence levels, or significance tests. The added plots do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The original tables and plotted results are retained. New Figures 14–19 report persistence of the two-stage pattern after high-norm filtering, early caption-to-answer information flow, factual-task results, and efficiency measurements. Appendix F reports approximately 40% lower inference time with largely preserved accuracy near the 20-layer setting; this is a new experiment, not a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The transformer definitions, attention-knockout formulation, probability projections, and Jaccard-similarity equation are unchanged. The added appendix material provides empirical procedures and interpretations without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central account: general visual integration precedes question-specific integration, followed by transfer to the answer position and later syntactic refinement. The new appendix evidence and application do not redefine these main scientific claims.

C2.justification: New discussion connects early visual-information transfer to efficient inference, contrasts caption and image processing, and explains that the original task selection avoided external-knowledge confounds. These add applicability arguments and qualifications while preserving the original mechanism interpretation.

D1.justification: The abstract newly provides a repository link and states that code and the collected dataset are released. Appendices E–F document the filtering threshold, average exclusion of 3.3 of 576 patches, token counts, and pruning depths. The new factual-task sampling details and timing hardware remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The main related-work discussion and 47-entry bibliography are retained. New appendix discussion invokes prior work on high-norm visual tokens and relates the unimodal findings to Geva et al. [19]. The high-norm-token and added dataset citations appear as unresolved question-mark references.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains unchanged, with localized grammar corrections and a release statement added to the abstract. Four appendix sections are inserted, and the subsequent sections and cross-references are renumbered; there is no extensive rewrite of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds six substantive figures: accuracy/runtime curves, a token-norm histogram, filtered-patch results, a caption comparison, and two factual-task panels. Existing Figures 14–31 become 20–37 without changed plots. Presentation weaknesses include missing task identifiers in Figures 16–17 and an ambiguous removal-depth axis in Figure 14, where runtime increases with the labeled number of removed layers.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the retained mechanism account with a targeted high-norm-token control and evidence beyond the selected GQA tasks. The efficiency experiment and code/data access statement also add usefulness. However, sparse documentation of the new evaluations, unresolved citations, and Figure 14's ambiguous axis limit the strength and reproducibility of these additions, making the net improvement limited.
